title: Decision Practice
subtitle: Stop & Decide prompts to build active clinical judgment
howToUse: These decision points interrupt passive reading and force active thinking. For each scenario, pause and write your response. Then compare with the model response. Focus on (1) the immediate risk, (2) the safest first nursing action, and (3) what data you must check next.

decisions.title: Hepatitis infection control
decisions.scenario: A patient with hepatitis B has jaundice and elevated liver enzymes.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelWhy: Hepatitis B is transmitted through blood and body fluids.
decisions.trap: Placing the patient in isolation unnecessarily.

decisions.title: Acute urinary retention
decisions.scenario: A patient reports severe suprapubic discomfort and inability to void for 10 hours.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Assess bladder distension and catheterize as ordered.
decisions.modelWhy: Urinary retention can cause kidney injury.

decisions.title: Prostate surgery complication
decisions.scenario: A patient post-TURP has bright red urine with clots and decreasing urine output.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Increase irrigation flow and notify the provider.
decisions.modelWhy: Clots can obstruct urine flow and cause bladder distension.

decisions.title: Ostomy care complication
decisions.scenario: A patient with a new colostomy has a stoma that appears dusky and pale.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Rheumatoid arthritis flare
decisions.scenario: A patient with rheumatoid arthritis reports sudden joint swelling, pain, and fever.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Assess for infection and notify the provider.
decisions.trap: Assuming it is a routine flare.

decisions.title: Systemic lupus erythematosus exacerbation
decisions.scenario: A patient with lupus presents with joint pain, rash, and decreased urine output.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Assess renal function and notify the provider.
decisions.modelWhy: Lupus nephritis can cause kidney failure.

decisions.title: Multiple sclerosis relapse
decisions.scenario: A patient with MS reports new onset of vision problems and limb weakness.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Notify the provider and prepare for corticosteroid therapy.
decisions.modelWhy: Relapses require prompt treatment to reduce inflammation.
decisions.trap: Assuming symptoms will resolve on their own.

decisions.title: ALS respiratory decline
decisions.scenario: A patient with ALS reports increasing shortness of breath and weak cough.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelFirst: Assess respiratory function and prepare for ventilatory support.
decisions.modelWhy: Respiratory muscle weakness is the leading cause of death in ALS.
